conviction_note: Findings offset: two sourced negatives on the line the stock trades on (the revenue bar sits at the top of the company's own H1 guide, and management's stated policy of reinvesting over-performance means a held EPS guide, which drew -10.2% last time) and a proxy tariff headwind, against an unquantified Phase 2 IEEPA refund that this company books into adjusted EPS and a 12.8%-of-float, 9-day short after a -9% five-day slide; p_up 47 x abs 14 gives -0.84, close to the -0.6 sum of the findings, and both are small against a 15% implied move because nothing here decides the print.
bar: Q2 FY27 consensus adjusted EPS $0.50-0.505 and revenue $443.2m, two agreeing sources: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-helen-of-troy-hele-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-01/ and https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/helen-of-troy-stock-heads-into-october-8-earnings-with-split-estimates/70206887. Company guide: Q2 roughly 15% of FY adjusted EPS $3.25-3.75, so $0.49-0.56, and H1 sales growth 'low to mid single digits' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/09/helen-of-troy-hele-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). The EPS bar sits inside the company's implied range. The revenue bar implies H1 +5.2%, at the top of it.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,952,013 shares, 12.77% of float, 9.0 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, roughly flat vs 2026-08-31 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HELE/short-interest/). Baseline skew_25d -2.27 vol points (calls bid slightly, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 1.32, event-implied move 14.95%, run-up -9.01% over 5d and -8.71% over 20d, 17.5% below the 52-week high. A crowded short with a mild call bid, after a slide on light volume with no identified cause (Oct 5: -5.8% on 66% below-average volume).

findings.finding: The consensus revenue bar of $443.2m implies H1 FY27 sales growth of +5.2% ($402.1m + $443.2m against $371.7m + $431.8m), at the top of the CFO's 'low to mid single digits' H1 guide. Q1 also pulled $4-5m of Prime Day orders out of Q2. The guide's midpoint (about +4%) implies Q2 revenue near $433-434m, roughly 2% under the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades on the EPS guide, not sales: Q1 FY27 beat revenue by about 7% and raised the sales guide, and the stock still fell 10.2% on 2026-07-08 (baseline). The company beat its own Q1 expectations by a wide margin, so it has a record of guiding conservatively.
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had anchored on the company's H1 cadence, consensus revenue would sit near $433m rather than $443m. Previews call the setup 'top-line growth versus earnings squeeze' and treat sales as the safe line.
findings.independence: Prior-year Q2 sales of $431.8m and Q1 FY27 sales of $402.1m come from the company's own releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916789/000091678926000094/fy27_q1xex-991.htm). The arithmetic rests on that and on the transcript; there is no independent corroboration of a miss.

findings.finding: IEEPA refund upside. Helen of Troy said it had paid $71m of IEEPA tariffs outside Phase 1, and that its adjusted EPS and EBITDA outlook includes refunds, though only the ~$9.2m Phase 1. The Q1 10-Q says CBP launched Phase 2 on 2026-06-29 and the company was preparing claims, with receivables booked once 'probable of being recovered'. Any Phase 2 acceptance by the Q2 close on Aug 31 lands in adjusted EPS against a $0.50 bar that excludes it (about $0.03 per $1m pre-tax on ~23m shares). CBP's Phase 3 went live on 2026-10-06.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund print on this name. The Q1 Phase 1 recognition ($1.8m pre-tax) was in the quarter that fell 10.2% on a held EPS guide. Peer Hamilton Beach booked $36.5m of refunds into its Apr-Jun quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001709164/000170916426000157/hbbhc63026earningsreleasee.htm).
findings.why_not_priced: The company told the street its guide excludes future refund phases, so consensus EPS of $0.50 sits inside the ex-Phase-2 cadence of $0.49-0.56. If refunds were priced, estimates would have moved up after Phase 2 launched; the visible revision path is Zacks moving $0.21 to $0.26 in July, still at or below the $0.50 consensus. Path to the guide is limited: management said it will 'deploy the bulk' of refunds back into the business, so this is sized as a one-off.
findings.independence: CBP's phase timeline is independent of the company (https://www.thompsoncoburn.com/insights/88-september-17-2026-cbp-confirms-launch-of-phase-3-of-ieepa-refund-process/), and Supply Chain Dive reports that the $71m awaits Phase 2 (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/osprey-brand-owner-says-high-supply-chain-costs-are-outpacing-ieepa-tariff/825081/). The Q2 amount is unknown, and the CFO said acceptance timing has no pattern 'we can reliably depend on'.

findings.finding: Management's stated policy is to reinvest 'the majority of over-performance back into the business' and 'the bulk' of refunds. Q1's beat therefore came with an unchanged adjusted EPS guide of $3.25-3.75, and the stock fell 10.2%. The same policy makes a held EPS guide the likely outcome again even if Q2 beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS guide moves drive this name: held guide after a beat -10.2% (2026-07-08), guide cuts -25.0% (2025-10-09) and -22.7% (2025-07-10), first FY27 guide +20.5% (2026-04-23), per the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is already 9% lower over five days and 17.5% off its high, and consensus FY EPS sits near or under the guide's low end. If the market fully expected a held guide, the call side would not be bid (skew -2.27).
findings.independence: Supply Chain Dive repeats the reinvestment plan (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/osprey-brand-owner-says-high-supply-chain-costs-are-outpacing-ieepa-tariff/825081/). It shares the transcript as its origin with the refund finding, but lands on a different line (the guide versus the quarter).

findings.finding: The FY27 guide assumes 'tariff rates in place as of June 2026' (Section 122 at 10%). From 2026-07-24, USTR's Section 301 action set China/Hong Kong and Vietnam at 12.5%: a 2.5-point increase on the main sourcing countries for most of FY27's second half, not in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff-driven guide cuts drew -22.7% (2025-07-10) and -25.0% (2025-10-09) per the baseline. This increment is far smaller.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate change is public, but the company has not quantified it. Consensus FY EPS has not visibly moved since July, and the guide's wide $0.50 range and the reinvestment buffer let it be absorbed. Macro-to-company transmission is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Proxy. The guide assumption is from the company release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000916789/000091678926000094/fy27_q1xex-991.htm). Hamilton Beach separately guided operating profit down high single digits ex-refunds on commodity and freight costs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001709164/000170916426000157/hbbhc63026earningsreleasee.htm).

findings.finding: YETI's Apr-Jun quarter showed US drinkware flat 'amid category competition', with a 600bp drag on 2026 US drinkware growth from fading trend SKUs. That is a soft read-through for Hydro Flask, one brand inside the Home & Outdoor segment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hydro Flask weakness was part of the FY26 sales declines that drew -22.7% and -25.0%. In Q1 FY27 Hydro Flask grew on distribution and Osprey was the strongest brand.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy on one brand. The rest of Home & Outdoor (OXO, Osprey) and all of Beauty & Wellness, more than half of sales, have to offset it, and in Q1 they did. Sized net of that.
findings.independence: YETI's own release covers the same quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001670592/000167059226000039/yeti-20260813xex991pressre.htm). There is no Hydro Flask-specific series.

findings.finding: Positioning: 12.77% of float short with 9.0 days to cover (2026-09-15), into a -9.0% five-day slide on light volume with no identified cause, while the 25-delta skew is -2.27 (calls bid). Any guide that is not cut has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one prior upside print (+20.5% on 2026-04-23, first FY27 guide) came with a large short base. Down prints have been large too, so shorts have not been punished every time.
findings.why_not_priced: The slide since Oct 1 ($27.41 to $24.94) came on 66% below-average volume (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-helen-of-troy-nasdaq-hele-stock-price-down-58-time-to-sell-2026-10-05/), which reads as no buyers rather than new information. The option market leans to the upside, not down.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -2.27 and the run-up are an independent source pointing the same way. The drawdown itself has no identified cause, so it carries no weight on its own.

outside_window.finding: CBP Phase 3 (entries liquidated more than 80 days ago, limited to importers with a CIT case pending) deployed 2026-10-06. Any cash from it for the rest of the $71m arrives over coming quarters, and the company has not said whether it has a CIT case. This is separate from any Q2 recognition, which is filed above.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks since 2026-07-08: only the 2026-08-26 annual-meeting 8-K (items 5.02 stock plan amendment, 5.07). No credit amendment, no pre-announcement, no exec departure
Form 4s 2026-09-02/04 (CEO Uzzell and others), consistent with Sept 1 anniversary vesting. No open-market purchase found
A cause for the -5.8% on 2026-10-05 and the gap down on 2026-10-06: no news, no analyst downgrade. Canaccord set a $26 target on 2026-10-06, above spot
Annual meeting 2026-08-25: no new trading commentary beyond the FY27 'foundation year' framing
Whether Helen of Troy has an IEEPA case pending at the CIT: not found in named-plaintiff lists
Retailer read-through (Walmart, Target, Amazon): nothing company-specific found; Prime Day phasing already disclosed by the company

lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, call skew): shrank the two company-document negatives (revenue bar, held guide) from -1.0 to -0.7 each

Rule 9 (net of the rest): shrank the YETI/Hydro Flask read-through from -0.3 to -0.2, since the other brands offset it in Q1
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): kept positioning as a finding under the core's filing rule but cut it from +1.0 to +0.7, carried by short interest and skew rather than the slide
Rule 2 (refund as one-off) and 'what has worked' (refund policy in a 10-Q matched to a disbursement window) pull in opposite directions; the refund finding stays at +1.0
